card.band: 20 h. This is a big surface with many features, so partial credit is steady. A frontier agent gets the core quickly, and secondary expansion, vpath, the odd functions and diagnostics message text are the long tail. Weaker models stop at basic rules. Risk: make is a crowded subject, so the scope is the complete test-suite behaviour and not just make basics.
card.cheat: GNU make is not installed in the image, so wrapping the real tool is impossible. Hidden Makefiles are not shipped, and exact messages cannot be guessed.
card.grading: Hidden: the 1210 run_make_test cases from tests/scripts, converted into a data-driven harness (Makefile, command line, expected output and exit code), plus generated Makefiles compared to the sealed real make. Tests are stdout/exit-status exact. Score is the fraction passed.
card.reference: The upstream GNU make is the oracle, and the reference solution is a compatible clone written for the task. Whether it reaches the ceiling is a risk: no permissive complete clone is verified (kati is incomplete), so the ceiling is the pass rate of our reference, not 1.
card.source: https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/make.git @ master b380278 (release tag not determined), GPL-3.0-or-later
card.task: /app ships a stub make binary skeleton and the written GNU make manual semantics list. Agent implements Makefile parsing, variable flavours, pattern and static rules, secondary expansion, the built-in function set, include and remake, .ONESHELL, -j with output sync, and the shell execution protocol.
card.title: GNU make 4.4 compatible build tool for the make test scripts

history: Make is on the CROWDED list, and gnu_make [SpecBench] is a public task with the same subject and deliverable (l0 cosine 0.271). The upstream tests are public, so the hidden corpus is recallable in outline. K1 applies.
source_notes: Each test is a Makefile + expected output in Perl heredocs, so porting the harness is needed or grader must keep Perl. Black-box 'implement make' is a classic but plausible; dependency on shell for recipes. Medium memorization risk
source_version: savannah master b380278 2026-04-29 (cloned; release tag not determined)

facts.claim: GNU make upstream repository exists with tests/scripts containing subdirectories features/, functions/, misc/, options/, targets/, variables/, vms/
tests/scripts contains 1210 test cases (per-directory file count not visible on the mirror page)
Upstream licence is GPL-3.0-or-later (COPYING fetch returned 502 on the Savannah host and was not visible on the mirror)
GNU make 4.4 was released on 31 October 2022
GNU make 4.4.1 bug-fix release came out on 26 February 2023
GNU make 4.4 tag exists in the upstream repository
kati is an incomplete GNU make-compatible clone (seed claim about its completeness)
remake is a GNU make fork packaged in Debian, built on GNU make's own code and targeting gnumake 3.81 compatibility, so not a from-scratch permissive clone
SpecBench lists a gnu_make task with a ~20K-line Python reference and 159 validation / 102 held-out tests

full_card.band: Seed claims 20 h; no dated public evidence of frontier results on this scope, so Band capped at 3.
full_card.build_cost: Reference is a full make-scale clone that passes 1210 exact-output tests: well over 5 days, so build cost is 1.
full_card.deliverable: Clone of GNU make 4.4 behaviour (parsing, variables, rules, functions, include/remake, .ONESHELL, -j output sync, shell protocol) scored on 1210 converted test cases.
full_card.gates_anticheat: No make binary in image so wrapping is impossible; hidden Makefiles unshipped. But upstream tests/scripts are public, so the case corpus is recallable in outline.
full_card.grading_surface: Hidden 1210 run_make_test cases from tests/scripts, exact stdout and exit code, plus generated Makefiles compared to real make.
full_card.local_fit: gVisor-compatible process and shell work; 8 CPU is enough; no network needed.
full_card.lookup: partial: make semantics are heavily memorised; a public gnu_make task (SpecBench) exists; no complete permissive clone verified.
full_card.provenance: GNU make upstream, git.savannah master b380278, release 4.4 (Oct 2022), GPL-3.0-or-later per seed (licence not directly verified).
full_card.reference: Upstream GNU make is the oracle; our reference is a task-written clone of unverified completeness; no permissive complete clone found (kati incomplete per seed, remake is a GPL fork).
full_card.ships: Stub make skeleton plus GNU make manual semantics list; no oracle or hidden Makefiles.
full_card.similarity: Same subject and deliverable as gnu_make [SpecBench] (cosine 0.271); make is on the CROWDED list; S-im-056 at 0.365 and S-im-048 at 0.292 are also close.

v1.kill_reason: Make is on the CROWDED list, and gnu_make [SpecBench] is a public task with the same subject and deliverable (l0 cosine 0.271). The upstream tests are public, so the hidden corpus is recallable in outline. K1 applies.

Band.why: Seed's 20 h band is asserted, with no dated public evidence; capped at 3.

Build.why: Reference equal to a full make clone passing 1210 cases is more than 5 days.

Fit.why: CPU-only and offline; process and shell tests fit gVisor.

Hor.why: Large surface suits a 20 h tier, though the long tail is much of the work.

Lic.why: GPL-3+ permits shipping, but the licence was not directly verified.

Multi.why: Test categories (features, functions, variables, targets, options) give steady buckets.

Nov.why: Same subject and deliverable as gnu_make [SpecBench] (0.271) on the CROWDED list.

Real.why: Upstream GNU make repo, 4.4 release (Oct 2022) and 4.4.1 confirmed; real tests/scripts tree exists.

Ref.why: No complete permissive clone verified; kati incomplete; our reference's ceiling is unknown.

Seal.why: Upstream tests are public and the GNU make source is recallable in outline, so the corpus is not sealed.

Surf.why: About 1210 exact-output cases, data-driven; large but not thousands of executable cases.

spike_plan.kill_if: Counts or determinism fail, or the tests cannot be converted without the Perl harness, or the public corpus makes the hidden cases recallable.
spike_plan.pass_if: Tests are deterministic over three runs, the count is about 1210, and the sampled features are separable into buckets a clone could pass independently.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone the upstream make repo at the pinned master commit and check tests/scripts file counts per directory against the claimed 1210.
Build upstream GNU make offline and run its test suite to confirm it is deterministic across three runs and records per-test pass/fail.
Sample 30 scripts across features/, functions/, targets/ and variables/, and estimate how many need -j output sync or shell-specific behaviour.
Check whether the 1210 cases can be converted to Makefile, command, expected stdout and exit code without the Perl harness.
Confirm the GPL-3.0-or-later COPYING text from a working mirror.
Check whether a licence-clean reference of 150 lines or more can cover the function set in one sitting.

v1.summary: The GNU make upstream repository, its 4.4 release and the tests/scripts layout are confirmed, but the 1210-case count, GPL licence and kati incompleteness are not verified. Because make is a crowded subject with a same-subject public neighbour (gnu_make [SpecBench]) and public tests, the idea is killed as K1 near-duplicate.
